from manim import *

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

class Section1Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Prerequisite: The Static Slope", ["Slope is the ratio of rise over run.", "Linear paths have a constant steepness.", "Rise over run defines a static slope."])
        
        # Initialize objects
        line = Line(self.grid["E5"] + LEFT*2, self.grid["B2"] + RIGHT*1, color=WHITE)
        label_m = MathTex(r"m = \frac{\Delta y}{\Delta x}", color="#FFD700")
        self.place_at_grid(label_m, "D4", scale_factor=1.2)
        
        point = Dot(color="#00FF00")
        path_point = ValueTracker(0)
        
        def update_point(p):
            p.move_to(line.point_from_proportion(path_point.get_value()))
            
        point.add_updater(update_point)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(line))
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(FadeIn(label_m))
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.add(point)
        self.play(path_point.animate.set_value(1), run_time=2)
        self.play(path_point.animate.set_value(0), run_time=2)
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFD700")
        self.wait(1)

class Section2Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("The Problem of Curves", ["Curves have changing slopes everywhere.", "Secant lines approximate local behavior.", "Tangent lines define exact local slope."])
        
        # Setup Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[-2, 2], y_range=[-1, 4], axis_config={"include_tip": False})
        axes.height = 4
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A2", "F5", scale_factor=0.8)
        
        parabola = axes.plot(lambda x: x**2, color="#00FFFF")
        
        # --- Assets ---
        # Note: /scratch/pawsey1357/jthen/Code2Video/assets/icon/none.svg is not a real asset to display,
        # skipping loading.

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"), Create(parabola))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        p1 = axes.c2p(-1.5, 2.25)
        p2 = axes.c2p(1, 1)
        secant = Line(p1, p2, color="#FFFF00")
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#FFFF00"), Create(secant))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Avoid using axes.get_tangent_line if it causes issues, build manually
        # Tangent line at x=0.5, y=0.25. Slope of x^2 is 2x, so slope at 0.5 is 1.

        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF00FF"), FadeOut(secant), Create(tangent))
        self.wait(2)

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lines = [
            "Zooming in reveals linear behavior.",
            "Curves locally behave like lines.",
            "Derivative is a local transformation.",
            "It captures instantaneous curve behavior.",
            "Magnification clarifies local steepness."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Transformational View (Zooming In)", lines)
        
        # Define objects
        curve = FunctionGraph(lambda x: 0.5 * x**2 + 0.2 * x, x_range=[-2, 2], color=BLUE)
        point = Dot(color=YELLOW)
        point.move_to(curve.point_from_proportion(0.6))
        
        # Area for animation
        self.place_in_area(curve, "B1", "E6")
        self.place_at_grid(point, "D3")
        
        # Animate
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(curve.animate.scale(2.0, about_point=point.get_center()))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        tangent_line = Line(start=LEFT*2, end=RIGHT*2, color=RED).rotate(PI/4).move_to(point.get_center())
        self.play(Create(tangent_line))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[3].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        arrow = Arrow(start=point.get_center(), end=point.get_center()+UP*1.5, color=GREEN)

        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[4].animate.set_color(YELLOW))

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Dynamic Application: The Cheetah's Sprint", [
            "Position graphs change over time.", 
            "Derivative yields velocity as slope.", 
            "Instantaneous speed is the derivative.", 
            "Acceleration shows rate of change.", 
            "Motion is captured by derivatives."
        ])
        
        # Colors for lecture lines
        colors = ["#FFD700", "#FF4500", "#00CED1", "#ADFF2F", "#DA70D6"]
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.lecture[0].set_color(colors[0])
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5], y_range=[0, 5], x_length=4, y_length=4)
        curve = axes.plot(lambda x: 0.2 * x**3, color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(axes, "A1", "D6", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.place_in_area(curve, "A1", "D6", scale_factor=0.7)
        self.add(axes, curve)
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.lecture[1].set_color(colors[1])
        dot = Dot(color=RED)
        dot.move_to(axes.c2p(2, 0.2 * 2**3))
        tangent = Line(start=LEFT, end=RIGHT, color=YELLOW).set_length(1)
        self.add(dot, tangent)
        
        def update_tangent(mob):
            x = (self.renderer.time * 0.5) % 4
            y = 0.2 * x**3
            dot.move_to(axes.c2p(x, y))
            slope = 0.6 * x**2
            angle = np.arctan(slope)
            mob.set_angle(angle)
            mob.move_to(dot.get_center())
        
        tangent.add_updater(update_tangent)
        self.wait(3)
        tangent.remove_updater(update_tangent)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.lecture[2].set_color(colors[2])
        speed_label = Text("Speed", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(speed_label, "E2")
        self.add(speed_label)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 4 ===
        self.lecture[3].set_color(colors[3])
        accel_label = Text("Acceleration", font_size=20, color=WHITE)
        self.place_at_grid(accel_label, "E5")
        self.add(accel_label)
        self.wait(2)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 5 ===
        self.lecture[4].set_color(colors[4])
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Derivatives extract local linear transformations.",
            "They simplify complex non-linear processes.",
            "Derivatives predict immediate future states."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("Summary & Conceptual Takeaway", lecture_lines)
        
        # Animation setup
        # Wavy curve (non-linear process)
        wavy_func = lambda t: 0.5 * np.sin(4 * t) + 0.2 * np.cos(10 * t)
        curve = FunctionGraph(wavy_func, x_range=[-1.5, 1.5], color=BLUE)
        self.place_in_area(curve, 'B2', 'D5')
        
        # Magnifying glass (a circle representing focus)
        magnifier = Circle(radius=0.5, color=YELLOW, stroke_width=4)
        self.place_at_grid(magnifier, 'C3')
        
        # Linear trend arrow
        arrow = Arrow(start=ORIGIN, end=RIGHT*1.5, color=RED)
        self.place_at_grid(arrow, 'C3')
        arrow.shift(RIGHT * 0.5)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE), Create(curve))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW), Create(magnifier))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(RED), FadeIn(arrow))
        self.wait(2)

outline.topic: The Transformational View of Derivatives: From Slopes to Dynamic Rates

sections.title: Prerequisite: The Static Slope
sections.content: Establish the foundation of a linear slope (m = Δy/Δx). Use a visual of a straight mountain path to demonstrate that the steepness is constant everywhere.
sections.example: A flat board resting on two blocks; the slope is the same whether you stand at the beginning or the end.

sections.title: The Problem of Curves
sections.content: Introduce a curved path (a parabola). Explain why 'rise over run' fails here because the slope changes at every point. Introduce the 'Secant Line' transitioning into a 'Tangent Line'.
sections.example: A roller coaster track. The slope at the bottom is different from the slope at the peak.

sections.title: The Transformational View (Zooming In)
sections.content: Define the derivative not as a static value, but as a local linear transformation. Explain that if we zoom in infinitely on a curve, it looks like a straight line. The derivative is the 'local instruction' for how the curve behaves at that specific coordinate.
sections.example: A tiny ant walking on a massive, curved watermelon; from the ant's perspective, the surface feels like a flat plane.

sections.title: Dynamic Application: The Cheetah's Sprint
sections.content: Apply the concept to motion. If 'position' is the curve, the 'derivative' is the velocity vector. Show how the derivative transforms the position graph into a real-time speed display.
sections.example: A cheetah chasing prey. The derivative captures the instantaneous speed at any precise second, even as the cheetah accelerates.

sections.title: Summary & Conceptual Takeaway
sections.content: Conclude that the derivative is a 'magnifying glass' that extracts a linear transformation from a complex non-linear process, allowing us to predict the next moment's state.
sections.example: Turning a complex, wavy 'stock market' graph into a simple arrow indicating the 'current direction' of the trend.
